chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, from whoever mentioned it, from Ali ibn al-Abbas, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, who said:
I described to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) the words of Hisham ibn Salim al-Jawaliqi, and I related to him the words of Hisham ibn al-Hakam that He (God) is a body.

So he said: Verily, God the Exalted — nothing resembles Him. What greater obscenity or turpitude exists than the words of one who describes the Creator of all things as having a body, or an image, or a creature-like nature, or a limitation, or body parts? Exalted is God above that, a great elevation.

key_terms.أعضاء: Body parts, limbs — physical members, whose attribution to God is rejected
key_terms.تحديد: Limitation, delimitation — ascribing finite boundaries to God
key_terms.جسم: Body, corporeal substance — the term used by Hisham ibn al-Hakam to describe God, rejected by the Imam
key_terms.خنا: Turpitude, treachery, baseness — used alongside fuhsh to describe the moral gravity of anthropomorphism
key_terms.عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا: A great elevation — Quranic phrase (17:43) affirming God's absolute transcendence
key_terms.فحش: Obscenity, abomination — a term for gross indecency, here applied to anthropomorphic theology

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Kazim say about describing God as having a body?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) responded to two divergent theological positions on God's nature — that of Hisham ibn Salim, who described God with some qualified anthropomorphism, and that of Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who explicitly said God is a body (jism). The Imam emphatically rejected all corporeal descriptions of God, citing the Quranic principle that nothing resembles Him, and condemned in the strongest terms the ascription of body, form, creaturely nature, limitation, or body parts to the Creator. This teaching situates al-Kazim within the Imami theological tradition of transcendent divine unity, which regards corporeal anthropomorphism as not merely mistaken but as a grave moral and religious offense.
